# spw_rmap_node: build brief

SpaceWire RMAP target: an OpenWire port and an OpenRMAP target with its memory interface.

This brief was generated by the Open Space Composer from the system file `spw_rmap_node.composer.json` (catalog `678558c4fcc6`).
The file holds the system as edited (`instances`, `connections`, `externals`), in `resolved` the netlist it resolves to and in `catalogSubset` the catalog entries of its blocks (interfaces, fields, clocks, generics).
Build a VHDL-2008 top level `spw_rmap_node` from `resolved` as described below; everything needed is in the file and in the listed repositories.

## 1. Sources and libraries

Fetch every repository at the given version and compile one VHDL-2008 library per row, in this order:

| Library | Repository | Version | Files | Entities used |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `olo` | https://github.com/open-space-hdl/open-logic-ft | tag `4.7.0-ft.3` (commit `a3c86207790fa91d89e5f02a657f6345de31656e`) | every file listed in `compile_order.txt`, in its order | `olo_base_reset_gen` |
| `openwire` | https://github.com/open-space-hdl/openwire | commit `2897668e2e519e9517a5c7270f243c5ab0d7fdb0` | every file listed in `compile_order.txt`, in its order | `owr_core` |
| `openrmap` | https://github.com/open-space-hdl/openrmap | commit `4ae4bfe31395ecbc31d5076796fd94bd7cb9de0e` | the `src/*.vhd` files of every module listed in `component_list.txt`, modules in the listed order | `omap_core` |

- `olo`: Clone with the submodule 3rdParty/en_cl_fix (git clone --recursive); compile_order.txt lists its files. 4.7.0-ft.3 adds olo_base_chunker and olo_axi_lite_decoder to 4.7.0-ft.2 and changes no other source, so the cores verified with 4.7.0-ft.2 use it unchanged.
- `openwire`: The submodules of the repository (open-logic, uvvm) serve its own tests; a system uses the olo library of the Composer.
- `openrmap`: The submodules of the repository (open-logic, uvvm) serve its own tests; a system uses the olo library of the Composer.
- One `olo` library (Open Logic FT `4.7.0-ft.3`) serves the whole system. The cores were verified with the Open Logic FT tags `4.7.0-ft.2` (openwire), `4.7.0-ft.2` (openrmap) (`verifiedWith`); their own `open-logic` submodules are not needed.
- A `modules` file list names one module directory per line, relative to the repository root; blank lines and lines starting with `#` are ignored. The sources of a module are its `src/*.vhd` files. Inside a module the files have no given order: compile its packages (`*_pkg.vhd`) first and let the tool order the rest (GHDL `-i` and `-m`, Vivado and VUnit do), or analyse them in dependency order.
- With GHDL: analyse Open Logic file by file (`ghdl -a --std=08 -frelaxed --work=olo <file>`), import the files of a core library (`ghdl -i --std=08 -frelaxed --work=<library> <files>`) and let `ghdl -m --std=08 -frelaxed <top>` find the order. `-frelaxed` is needed: Open Logic and the cores use constructs that GHDL accepts only relaxed (for example the shared variable of `olo_base_ram_sdp`).
- With other tools follow the order of the table.

External interfaces:

- `spw0.S_AxiLite` (AXI4-Lite register bus, clock domain `sys`): AXI4-Lite register access (32 bit data), for example the register file of a core.
- `spw0.Spw` (SpaceWire line, clock domain `link`): Data-strobe line drivers and receivers of a SpaceWire link (LVDS buffers outside the core).
- `rmap0.S_AxiLite` (AXI4-Lite register bus, clock domain `sys`): AXI4-Lite register access (32 bit data), for example the register file of a core.
- `rmap0.M_Axi` (AXI4 memory bus, clock domain `sys`): AXI4 memory-mapped bus (bursts), for example the memory access of an RMAP target.

## 3. Architecture

1. Context clause (`resolved.context`): `library ieee;` `use ieee.std_logic_1164.all;` `library olo;` `library openwire;` `library openrmap;`
2. Declare every signal of `resolved.signals` (one per port of an instance, named `<instance>_<port>_s`, with the type of the port).
3. Instantiate every entry of `resolved.instances` as `<id> : entity <library>.<entity>`: a generic map with the generics whose `default` is false (the value is the VHDL literal in `vhdl`), and a port map with the `actual` of every port. Leave out the ports with `useDefault` (they keep their VHDL `default`). Clocks and resets are port actuals on purpose: never assign a clock to another signal.
4. Write every entry of `resolved.nets` as a concurrent assignment `<to> <= <from>;`. They connect the interfaces signal by signal (a packed data word bit by bit), set the side band constants and tie-offs, and connect the top-level ports.

| Instance | Entity | Library | Origin | Clock domain | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spw0` | `owr_core` | `openwire` | placed | sys |  |
| `rmap0` | `omap_core` | `openrmap` | placed | sys |  |
| `auto_rst_sys` | `olo_base_reset_gen` | `olo` | inserted: reset | sys | Synchronous reset of System clock. |

Generics that differ from the VHDL default:

- `spw0`: `LinkClkFreq_g => 200.0e6`, `RunDiv_g => 2`
- `rmap0`: `Initiator_g => false`
- `auto_rst_sys`: `SyncTmr_g => true`

## 4. Clocks and resets

| Clock domain | Frequency | Clock | Reset generator |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| System clock (`sys`) | 100 MHz | top-level port `Clk_sys` | `auto_rst_sys` (olo_base_reset_gen, output `auto_rst_sys_RstOut_s`) |
| Link clock (`link`) | 200 MHz | top-level port `Clk_link` | none: no block of the domain has a synchronous reset |

Reset ports (`reset` of the port):

| Port | Reset | Actual | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spw0.Rst` | asynchronous | `Rst` | Asynchronous reset; the core synchronises its release in every domain. |
| `rmap0.Rst` | synchronous | `auto_rst_sys_RstOut_s` | Synchronous reset in the clock domain System clock (clock Clk): the output of the reset generator auto_rst_sys. |
| `auto_rst_sys.RstIn` | asynchronous | `Rst` | Asynchronous reset input (polarity from RstInPolarity_g). |

`Rst` is the asynchronous system reset. A reset generator asserts the reset of its domain at once and releases it synchronously to the clock; a block with an asynchronous reset synchronises the release itself.

## 5. Constraints

Every clock crossing is an Open Logic block. Between the clocks of a crossing a maximum delay applies in both directions, the period of the faster clock, data path only (Open Logic clock crossing principles). Do not declare these clocks as asynchronous clock groups: in Vivado `set_clock_groups -asynchronous` overrides the delay limits.

- False path from `Rst`: Asynchronous reset input; the reset generators synchronise its release.
- False path from `spw0_Spw_DIn`, `spw0_Spw_SIn`: Inputs that spw0 synchronises itself.
- Output registers in the I/O blocks for `spw0_Spw_DOut`, `spw0_Spw_SOut`: Place the output flip-flops of data and strobe in the I/O blocks with matched routing.
- Maximum delay from the clock of `Clk_link` to the clock of `Clk_sys`: 5 ns, data path only (`set_max_delay -datapath_only` in Vivado). Clock crossings of spw0: the period of the faster clock.
- Maximum delay from the clock of `Clk_sys` to the clock of `Clk_link`: 5 ns, data path only (`set_max_delay -datapath_only` in Vivado). Clock crossings of spw0: the period of the faster clock.
- AMD Vivado: source the script of Open Logic once. It reads the scoped constraints of olo_base_cc_reset, olo_base_cc_bits, olo_base_cc_simple, olo_base_reset_gen and olo_base_ram_sdp wherever the system uses them, also inside the cores. tools/vivado/all_constraints_amd.tcl would also read those of olo_intf_sync, which expect device pins at its input and stop the build (ERROR 18-513) where a block synchronises internal signals with it, as ofb_pa_gty does; a block that synchronises device pins declares its own false path for them. File `src/base/tcl/olo_base_constraints_amd.tcl` of Open Logic.

## 6. Notes from the user guides

**SpaceWire port** (`owr_core`, `spw0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openwire/docs/user_guide.html

- LVDS output buffers for data and strobe and LVDS input buffers with fail-safe biasing belong to the top level; the core contains no I/O buffer.
- Enable the safe implementation of state machines in the synthesis tool.
- Set INT_HOLDOFF and INT_ACK_DELAY for the network before distributed interrupts are used.
- Serve the indication ports before the indication FIFO (16 entries) fills.
- Write registers as 32-bit words; a read that depends on a write waits for the write response.

**RMAP node** (`omap_core`, `rmap0`): https://openspacehdl.org/openrmap/docs/user_guide.html

- Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen.
- M_RepData, M_Conf and M_User must be served when connected; a stalled output stalls the received packet stream and the link.
- RMAP address bits above AxiAddrWidth_g must be zero in the windows.
- With AxiMaxBeats_g = 1 and AxiDataWidth_g = 32 the memory master issues single transfers only and can drive an AXI4-Lite slave; tie M_Axi_RLast to '1'. Known defect of the pinned version (fix in progress in OpenRMAP): with AxiMaxBeats_g < 4, commands longer than one AXI transaction return or write wrong data.

## 7. Initialisation by software

Register addresses are byte addresses of the AXI4-Lite port of the block; write registers as 32-bit words and wait for the write response before a read that depends on it.

**`spw0`** (SpaceWire port, `owr_core`) through the top-level ports `spw_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x00): it reads 0x4F575201.
2. Optionally write LINK_SPEED (0x14) bits 7:0 RUN_DIV: the bit period in the Run state in LinkClk cycles (reset value RunDiv_g); choose it for the far end, which samples at most about LinkClk / 1.2.
3. Write PORT_CTRL (0x10) = 0x34 (RECEIVER_EN, DRIVER_EN, LINK_START) to start the link, or 0x38 (AUTO_START) to wait for the far end.
4. Wait for PORT_STATUS (0x18) bits 2:0 LINK_STATE = 5 (Run) before packets are exchanged.

**`rmap0`** (RMAP node, `omap_core`) through the top-level ports `rmap_reg_S_AxiLite_*`:

1. Read ID (0x000): it reads 0x4F4D4101.
2. None needed: with the default generics the target accepts every command to the logical address 0xFE with the key 0x00 on the whole address space (WinInit_g). A flight configuration narrows the logical addresses (TGT_LA 0x010), the key (TGT_KEY) and the windows (WIN_BASE, WIN_LAST, WIN_CTRL), see the register map.

## 8. Checks

No problems found.

## 9. Verification

A smoke testbench `spw_rmap_node_tb` (VHDL-2008, no extra libraries):

1. Instantiate `spw_rmap_node` and drive `Clk_sys` at 100 MHz, `Clk_link` at 200 MHz.
2. Hold `Rst` at '1' for 16 cycles of the slowest clock (100 MHz), then '0'.
3. Keep every external input idle: stream inputs with valid at '0', ready inputs of external outputs at '1', bus requests idle, pins at '0'.
4. Run for at least 100 us (the blocks initialise their tables after the reset) and stop the simulation: it must end without failed assertions, and the handshake outputs of the top level (valid, ready) and the line outputs must not be 'U' or 'X' after the reset. Data outputs may stay undefined while their valid is '0'.
5. Where an AXI4-Lite port is external, read the ID register of the block (section 7) and compare it with the documented value.

With GHDL: analyse the libraries of section 1, then `ghdl -i --std=08 -frelaxed spw_rmap_node.vhd spw_rmap_node_tb.vhd`, `ghdl -m --std=08 -frelaxed spw_rmap_node_tb` and `ghdl -r --std=08 -frelaxed spw_rmap_node_tb --stop-time=100us --assert-level=error --ieee-asserts=disable` (`--ieee-asserts=disable` silences the warnings of the numeric package about metavalues before the reset).

Optional end-to-end test, after the initialisation of section 7:

- SpaceWire port (`owr_core`): Loop the SpaceWire line back (Spw_DOut to Spw_DIn, Spw_SOut to Spw_SIn) or connect a second port, start the link and wait for PORT_STATUS LINK_STATE = 5 (Run).

blocks.name: SpaceWire port
blocks.summary: SpaceWire port according to ECSS-E-ST-50-12C Rev.1: encoding, data link and network services (packets, time-codes, distributed interrupts) with a register file.
notes: LVDS output buffers for data and strobe and LVDS input buffers with fail-safe biasing belong to the top level; the core contains no I/O buffer.
Enable the safe implementation of state machines in the synthesis tool.
Set INT_HOLDOFF and INT_ACK_DELAY for the network before distributed interrupts are used.
Serve the indication ports before the indication FIFO (16 entries) fills.
Write registers as 32-bit words; a read that depends on a write waits for the write response.

rules.message: A receiver samples a bit period that is longer than 1.2 of its LinkClk periods (user guide, section 3)

constraints.note: Clock crossings inside the core (Open Logic FT FIFOs and synchronisers): for every pair of its clocks, in both directions, the period of the faster clock; no asynchronous clock groups.
Place the output flip-flops of data and strobe in the I/O blocks with matched routing.

init.text: Optionally write LINK_SPEED (0x14) bits 7:0 RUN_DIV: the bit period in the Run state in LinkClk cycles (reset value RunDiv_g); choose it for the far end, which samples at most about LinkClk / 1.2.
Write PORT_CTRL (0x10) = 0x34 (RECEIVER_EN, DRIVER_EN, LINK_START) to start the link, or 0x38 (AUTO_START) to wait for the far end.
The link starts after the reset without software (LinkStart_g or AutoStart_g).
The link starts after the reset without software (LinkStart_g or AutoStart_g).
Wait for PORT_STATUS (0x18) bits 2:0 LINK_STATE = 5 (Run) before packets are exchanged.

blocks.endToEnd: Loop the SpaceWire line back (Spw_DOut to Spw_DIn, Spw_SOut to Spw_SIn) or connect a second port, start the link and wait for PORT_STATUS LINK_STATE = 5 (Run).

generics.name: LinkClkFreq_g
generics.label: Link clock frequency
generics.description: Frequency of LinkClk. It must lie within 10 % of a multiple of 10 MHz, so that 10 Mb/s +/- 10 % can be reached with an integer divider.

generics.name: TxFifoDepth_g
generics.label: Transmit FIFO depth
generics.description: Depth of the transmit FIFO in N-Chars (power of 2).

generics.name: RxFifoDepth_g
generics.label: Receive FIFO depth
generics.description: Depth of the receive FIFO in N-Chars (power of 2); 64 or more allows seven outstanding FCTs.

generics.name: TimeCodes_g
generics.label: Time-code service
generics.description: Enables the time-code service and its ports.

generics.name: Interrupts_g
generics.label: Interrupt service
generics.description: Enables the distributed interrupt service and its ports.

generics.name: IntTimerWidth_g
generics.label: Interrupt timer width
generics.description: Width of the minimum interval and acknowledgement delay of the interrupt service

generics.name: LinkDisabled_g
generics.label: Link disabled after reset
generics.description: Reset value of LinkDisabled.

generics.name: LinkStart_g
generics.label: Link start after reset
generics.description: Reset value of LinkStart; the port starts the link without software.

generics.name: AutoStart_g
generics.label: Auto start after reset
generics.description: Reset value of AutoStart; the port starts the link when the far end does.

generics.name: RunDiv_g
generics.label: Run divider
generics.description: Reset value of the bit period in the Run state in LinkClk cycles.

generics.name: SyncStages_g
generics.label: Synchroniser stages
generics.description: Synchroniser stages of data and strobe.

clocks.label: User
clocks.description: Packet and broadcast service ports (any frequency).

clocks.label: Link
clocks.description: Encoding and data link layers; the transmit bit period is n LinkClk periods (n = 1 to 255).

resets.description: Asynchronous reset; the core synchronises its release in every domain.

interfaces.name: M_Pkt
interfaces.label: Received packets
interfaces.description: Must be served; the port gives credit only for free places of the receive FIFO.

blocks.name: RMAP node
blocks.summary: RMAP target and initiator according to ECSS-E-ST-50-52C on SpaceWire packet ports, with a memory master, a pass-through port for other protocols and a register file.
notes: Rst is synchronous and high-active; synchronise its release to Clk, for example with olo_base_reset_gen.
M_RepData, M_Conf and M_User must be served when connected; a stalled output stalls the received packet stream and the link.
RMAP address bits above AxiAddrWidth_g must be zero in the windows.

With AxiMaxBeats_g = 1 and AxiDataWidth_g = 32 the memory master issues single transfers only and can drive an AXI4-Lite slave; tie M_Axi_RLast to '1'. Known defect of the pinned version (fix in progress in OpenRMAP): with AxiMaxBeats_g < 4, commands longer than one AXI transaction return or write wrong data.

rules.message: At least one of Target_g and Initiator_g must be true.
Two nodes that are initiator and target of each other on one link need Transactions_g = 1.
The RMAP node normally runs on the user clock of its SpaceWire port; an asynchronous FIFO was inserted instead.
Known defect: commands longer than one AXI transaction return or write wrong data with AxiMaxBeats_g < 4; fix in progress in OpenRMAP.

init.text: None needed: with the default generics the target accepts every command to the logical address 0xFE with the key 0x00 on the whole address space (WinInit_g). A flight configuration narrows the logical addresses (TGT_LA 0x010), the key (TGT_KEY) and the windows (WIN_BASE, WIN_LAST, WIN_CTRL), see the register map.

generics.name: Target_g
generics.label: Target
generics.description: The node executes RMAP commands (ECSS 5.7.1). At least one of Target and Initiator.

generics.name: Initiator_g
generics.label: Initiator
generics.description: The node issues RMAP commands (ECSS 5.7.1). At least one of Target and Initiator.

generics.name: Passthrough_g
generics.label: Pass-through port
generics.description: User port for packets of other protocols; without it they are discarded and counted.

generics.name: AxiAddrWidth_g
generics.label: Memory address width
generics.description: Address width of the memory interface; RMAP address bits above it must be zero.

generics.name: AxiDataWidth_g
generics.label: Memory data width
generics.description: Data width of the memory interface (power of 2); the memory word of single-address accesses.

generics.name: AxiMaxBeats_g
generics.label: Maximum burst length
generics.description: Maximum burst length of the memory interface; 1 makes the memory master usable as AXI4-Lite master.

generics.name: BufferBytes_g
generics.label: Write buffer
generics.description: Maximum Data Length of a verified write.

generics.name: ChunkBytes_g
generics.label: Write chunk
generics.description: Chunk of a non-verified write that is written to memory once it is complete in the buffer.

generics.name: Windows_g
generics.label: Address windows
generics.description: Address windows of the target.

generics.name: ExtAuth_g
generics.label: External authorisation
generics.description: Every command that passes the internal checks is presented for authorisation.

generics.name: TgtAddrBytes_g
generics.label: Target address bytes
generics.description: Maximum length of the target SpaceWire address of a request.

generics.name: Transactions_g
generics.label: Transactions
generics.description: Entries of the transaction table of the initiator; 0 without table and timeout.

generics.name: La0_g
generics.label: Logical address 0
generics.description: Reset value of logical address 0 of the target (enabled after reset).

generics.name: La1_g
generics.label: Logical address 1
generics.description: Reset value of logical address 1 of the target (disabled after reset).

generics.name: DefLaEn_g
generics.label: Default address enabled
generics.description: Reset value of the enable of the default logical address 0xFE.

generics.name: Key_g
generics.label: Key
generics.description: Reset value of the key of the target.

generics.name: TickCycles_g
generics.label: Tick period
generics.description: Reset value of the tick period minus one

generics.name: Timeout_g
generics.label: Reply timeout
generics.description: Reset value of the reply timeout in ticks; 0 disables it.

generics.name: WinInit_g
generics.label: Initial windows
generics.description: Reset values of the windows (WinCfgArray_t of omap_pkg); window 0 open by default.

clocks.label: Clock
clocks.description: All of the core; one character per cycle.

interfaces.name: M_User
interfaces.label: Other protocols out
interfaces.description: Packets whose second character is not the protocol identifier 0x01; unconnected, every packet is accepted.

interfaces.name: S_User
interfaces.label: Other protocols in
interfaces.description: Packets of other protocols, sent unchanged between the RMAP packets.

presets.name: RMAP target
presets.summary: Executes RMAP commands on its memory interface; no initiator.

presets.name: RMAP initiator
presets.summary: Issues RMAP commands and receives the replies; no target.

blocks.name: Reset generator
blocks.summary: Synchronises an asynchronous reset to a clock and stretches it; optionally triplicated synchronisers.
